period: Legendary figure; no historical dating is possible.
context: Kapila is honoured as the founding sage of Sankhya, but he is a legendary rather than a historically documented figure. No work that can be securely ascribed to him survives. The Sankhya Karika names a line of teachers descending from Kapila through Asuri and Panchashikha. The Bhagavata Purana presents a Kapila, regarded as an incarnation of Vishnu, teaching a devotional form of Sankhya to his mother Devahuti, and the Bhagavad Gita names Kapila among perfected sages (10.26). Whether these references point to one figure is unclear.
coreIdeas: In tradition, the first teacher of the distinction between consciousness (purusha) and nature (prakriti)
Liberation through discriminating knowledge of this distinction
Enumeration of the principles (tattvas) through which nature unfolds
In the Bhagavata Purana, Sankhya analysis joined with devotion to God
otherWorks: Sankhya Sutras (traditionally attributed; generally dated much later, around the 14th–15th century CE)
Teaching to Devahuti in the Bhagavata Purana, Canto 3 (a Puranic presentation)
attributionNote: Texts bearing Kapila's name are traditional attributions to a legendary founder and are much later than the origins of Sankhya.
